title: Probing-based KV residency calibrator and memory profile optimizer for long-context Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants
creator: Rui Chen
description: Implement a lightweight probing-based KV residency calibration service that builds per-variant, per-layer residency curves during low-utilization windows and integrates the resulting profiles with continuous batching and the slab allocator. The goal is to reduce peak GPU memory and fragmentation for long-context Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants while keeping token-latency and model quality within SLOs. This ticket covers: 1) probe design and safe sampling (non-invasive, low-overhead), 2) residency curve fitting and hysteresis to prevent oscillation, 3) a runtime hook that exposes residency hints to the batch coalescer and slab compactor, and 4) a small A/B experiment harness for evaluating memory, latency, and throughput trade-offs.
acceptance_criteria: Profiling probe overhead < 1.5% p99 CPU during sampling windows
Per-variant residency curves generated and stored in the memory profile catalog
Integrated hints reduce peak GPU memory by >= 6% on average for long-context workloads (>= 8k tokens) across Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants in our benchmark suite
No regression in median generation latency > 5% and p99 latency within SLO for canary traffic
Automated rollout flag and fallback path if residency-guided packing increases OOM rate
comments: 2026-02-10 - Rui Chen: Initial RFC posted. Proposal: run 30s probes during scheduled low-load windows per GPU that iterate a small synthetic KV access pattern across the top N layers to estimate eviction sensitivity.
2026-02-14 - Aisha Malik: Reviewed RFC. Concern: noisy probes may interact badly with concurrent prefetch. Proposal accepted to add exponential backoff and alignment with existing prefetch windows.
2026-02-18 - Marco Alvarez (infra): Implemented the first probe harness in staging. Early numbers look promising — sampling adds ~0.9% CPU during the 30s window and negligible memory churn.
2026-02-24 - ML infra: Fitting residency curves using a three-parameter logistic model produced stable per-layer thresholds for Llama-70B longctx variant. Uploading sample CSV to Confluence.

2026-03-01 - SRE: End-to-end canary run with residency hints enabled for qwen-34b-longctx on 4 nodes. Peak memory down 7.8% avg; one spike at 03:42 UTC caused p99 latency to jump 9% — investigation points to batch coalescer not applying hysteresis.

2026-03-03 - Aisha Malik: Added hysteresis to residency application (moving-average + min-apply-delay) and a safety gate to prevent changing packing within a pre-configured warmup window. Re-ran canary.
2026-03-08 - Performance: Canary re-run results: peak memory down 8.9% across workloads; median latency unchanged, p99 reduced to +3% (within SLO). Documented canary artifacts in attachments.
2026-03-10 - Security: Confirmed probes do not access customer prompt contents and only operate on internal KV indices. Security review not required for this phase.

2026-03-12 - Aisha Malik: Open PR created for the runtime hooks and profile uploader. Moving to In Progress for production hardening and additional model variants. Next: expand sampling matrix (sequence lengths, quantization modes).
notes: Design trade-offs: aggressive residency trimming reduces fragmentation but can increase latency due to increased prefetch misses; we use a cost model to bound changes.
Implementation detail: residency curves are stored as small (layer, threshold, slope) tuples in the catalog to keep the profile compact and fast to apply at runtime.
Integration: batching will treat residency hints as soft constraints; when incompatible with latency SLOs, the optimizer will prefer latency.
Future work: extend to multi-tenant eviction policies, and investigate combining with quantization-specific slab pinning for QAT/INT8 variants.
